recommendation: Keep the commit. A future publisher enhancement could render abstract Resource operation URLs as [ResourceType] directly, but this source clarification fixes the current implementer-facing ambiguity without conflicting with later system-level $validate support.
issue_request: FHIR-37626 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I technical correction asking the Resource $validate operation URL examples to use [resourceType] and [resourceType]/[id] rather than literal Resource paths.
initial_application: No explicit source commit mentioning FHIR-37626 was found. The current generated formal OperationDefinition narrative still displays Resource in type and instance URL lines, and the source lacked local prose explaining that Resource is an abstract placeholder in those paths.
additional_context: The original Zulip thread confirms that Resource was not intended to be a literal endpoint. Later FHIR-41356 added valid system-level [base]/$validate support, and FHIR-41357 added a validate invocation matrix, so this reconciliation is scoped to type- and instance-level paths and does not remove system-level invocation.
reconciliation: Updated source/resource/operationdefinition-Resource-validate.xml in the footer markdown and OperationDefinition comment to state that type- and instance-level invocations use concrete resource types such as Patient and that /Resource/$validate and /Resource/[id]/$validate are not literal endpoints.
source_changes: source/resource/operationdefinition-Resource-validate.xml: added concrete-resource-type clarification to the build footer markdown and OperationDefinition comment.

related_jiras.note: Added system-level [base]/$validate support, so the FHIR-37626 clarification must be limited to type- and instance-level paths. Already represented on the combined branch.
